papers.title: From divergence to convergence: GenAI's role in collaborative design thinking
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) offers significant potential to boost innovation performance by accelerating speed and productivity. However, its integration into collaborative, empathy-driven processes like design thinking remains a complex challenge. Drawing on qualitative data from three innovation sprints involving 71 interdisciplinary teams and 18 corporate partners, we investigate how GenAI impacts the core design phases of problem understanding, ideation, and prototyping. Our findings demonstrate that while GenAI effectively expands the problem space and generates diverse solutions, its integration varies significantly across teams. We identify a critical tension: although GenAI can enhance early-stage divergence, its output often lacks the contextual and empathic depth required for user-centered innovation. To address this, we propose a 2x2 framework defined by two dimensions – Level of Integration (High vs. Low) and Purpose of Use (Supportive vs. Directive) – identifying four distinct engagement patterns. This typology illustrates the trade-offs between productivity and team-based empathy and coordination, providing a nuanced perspective on how AI reshapes different stages of the design process. Finally, we offer practical guidance on team orchestration and intervention strategies to ensure GenAI augments, rather than undermines, collaborative creativity.
papers.summary_ja: GenAIをデザイン思考の発散・収束プロセスに統合した際の効果と限界を、71チーム・18企業を対象とした実証研究で明らかにし、チーム別の4つのエンゲージメントパターン（統合レベル×使用目的の2×2フレームワーク）を提示する。

papers.title: Service-Dominant Logic in the AI Era
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) reflects its widespread adoption across various industries and occupations. Yet, much of the discourse still conceptualizes AI narrowly as a property of computational machinery. Within marketing and service scholarship, such mechanistic framings obscure the relational and systemic dimensions of intelligence that become salient in AI-enabled service interactions. Drawing on service-dominant (S-D) logic, this paper reconceptualizes intelligence as an emergent property of adaptive, self-organizing service ecosystems, foregrounding the systemic processes and relational configurations through which actors and their capacities take form. As intelligent technologies become increasingly entangled in service exchange, they render more visible and consequential the ongoing interactions through which human and non-human actors are co-constituted, underscoring the need for a clearer relational-ontological grounding of S-D logic. We conceptualize adaptation and intelligence as a generative duality: adaptation captures the adjustments enacted within a service ecosystem, whereas intelligence denotes the systemic capacity enabling those adjustments through feedback, learning, and institutional co-evolution. This perspective strengthens S-D logic's relational foundations by showing that AI exemplifies—rather than disrupts—the emergent, relational processes through which service ecosystems coordinate, evolve, and create value.
papers.summary_ja: サービス支配論理（SDL）の創始者Vargoが、AIを計算機械の属性としてではなくサービスエコシステムの創発的・関係的プロセスとして再概念化し、「適応と知性の生成的二重性」という新たな理論的基盤を提示する。

papers.title: Connecting Thoughts and Actions: A Managerial Process Model on Circular Business Model Innovation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Addressing environmental grand challenges such as resource scarcity requires circular business model innovation (CBMI) that enables firms to efficiently close and slow resource cycles through novel activity systems. Drawing on a grounded theory approach based on 59 in-depth interviews with top managers from Swiss SMEs, we developed a process model that explains how cognitive and behavioral managerial antecedents interact to drive CBMI. Anchored in dynamic capability (DC) theory, the model conceptualizes CBMI as a three-phase process and identifies six key managerial antecedents. We show how perceived environmental embeddedness and collaborative ideation support the sensing of circular opportunities, how foresighted thrift and cultivating organizational change enable the seizing of resources, and how enduring commitment and continuous experimentation drive business model reconfiguration. We contribute to the CBMI literature by advancing a processual understanding of managerial agency and applying DC theory to explicate the cognitive-behavioral dynamics through which DCs are activated and sustained.
papers.summary_ja: スイスのSME経営幹部59名へのインタビューに基づくグラウンデッドセオリーで、循環型ビジネスモデルイノベーション（CBMI）を「感知→獲得→再構成」の3フェーズプロセスとして捉え、6つの主要経営者先行条件を特定した動的ケイパビリティモデルを提示する。

papers.title: How does strategic foresight enhance policy capacities in the governance of grand challenges?
papers.abstract: This paper analyses the potential of Strategic foresight (SF) in tackling non-linear and long-term policy problems, using grand challenges as the unit of analysis. While the strengths of SF are well understood, so far the theorisation of its governance capabilities has been limited by an empirical focus on piecemeal applications that are disjointed from governance systems. This paper addresses this gap by examining the conditions under which SF enhances policy capacities in the governance of grand challenges.
papers.summary_ja: グランドチャレンジの統治における戦略的フォーサイトの政策能力強化メカニズムを分析し、非線形・長期的政策課題へのSF活用の理論的基盤を提供する。

papers.title: Bridging human and machine intelligence: How design thinking and generative AI capabilities drive exploratory and exploitative innovation
papers.summary_ja: デザイン思考とGenerative AIのケイパビリティが探索的イノベーション（exploration）と深化的イノベーション（exploitation）をどのように促進するかを実証的に解明し、人間と機械の知性統合の理論的基盤を提示する。

papers.title: Strategic responses of platform multinational enterprises: Rethinking competition policy through a comparative institutional perspective
papers.abstract: As of 2026, the battle continues between competition and regulatory policies over whether—and how much—to rein in online digital platforms. These debates have gained renewed urgency given the growing entanglement of major U.S.-based platforms with domestic political elites. The global responses of multinational platform firms (platform MNEs) further complicate this conflict. Existing research has largely focused on single-country regulatory frameworks, missing the comparative dimension that shapes platform MNE strategy.
papers.summary_ja: 各国の競争政策の違いに対するプラットフォームMNEの戦略的対応を比較制度論で分析し、規制環境がデジタルプラットフォーム企業の行動をどう形成するかを明らかにする。

papers.title: Building industry in 2040: An explorative scenario analysis of alternative sustainability pathways
papers.abstract: The building industry is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions in Europe and, with low productivity growth and fragmentation, has failed to create sufficient affordable, livable and sustainable housing. The EU Green Deal, digitalization, circularity, labor shortages, and industrialization are among the key forces expected to reshape the industry in the coming decades. How this change will unfold is, however, deeply uncertain.
papers.summary_ja: 欧州建設業の2040年に向けた持続可能性トランジションの代替シナリオをRohrbeckが探索的に構築し、デジタル化・サーキュラリティ・脱炭素化の複合的影響と不確実性を分析する。

papers.title: When creation and capture diverge: Why breakthrough inventions do not break through alike
papers.abstract: Breakthrough inventions are central to firms' competitive advantage, yet what constitutes a breakthrough remains unclear. We examine the relationship between technological quality (measured by forward citations) and economic value (measured by grant-day abnormal stock-returns) of patents. Using U.S. patents assigned to publicly listed firms, we find that among the most exceptional inventions, technological quality and economic value systematically diverge.
papers.summary_ja: 技術的品質（被引用数）と経済的価値（株式リターン）の両方が高い発明でも価値獲得パターンが大きく異なることを特許データで実証し、ブレークスルー発明の「創造と獲得の乖離」メカニズムを解明する。

papers.title: Dynamic capabilities for co-innovation in timber construction: a case study of Swedish cross laminated timber innovation ecosystems
papers.abstract: Introduction Despite growing recognition of engineered wood products as a critical enabler of low-carbon and circular construction, the diffusion of cross laminated timber (CLT) remains comparatively slow relative to its technical maturity and sustainability potential. This suggests that timber adoption is shaped not only as a design challenge but also by firms' capabilities, collaborative practices, and ecosystem-level factors.
papers.summary_ja: スウェーデンのCLT（クロスラミネーティッドティンバー）イノベーションエコシステムのケーススタディを通じ、建設業における共同イノベーションを支える動的ケイパビリティと協働実践を特定する。

papers.title: Sustainability-Driven Digital Transformation and Customer Experience in Emerging Markets: The Interplay of Business Model Innovation and Value Co-Creation
papers.abstract: Service industries are fast turning digital, and they are disrupting the manner in which firms organize and relate to their customers. Nevertheless, mechanisms that allow digital capabilities to be converted to better customer experience remain poorly understood, especially in the emerging economies. This paper presents the dual-mediation model to investigate the effects of Digital Supply Chain Integration and Digital Process Innovation on customer experience, with Business Model Innovation and Value Co-Creation as mediators.
papers.summary_ja: 新興市場におけるサステナビリティ主導のデジタルトランスフォーメーションが顧客体験に与える影響を、ビジネスモデルイノベーションと価値共創を媒介変数としたデュアルメディエーションモデルで実証する。
